commands.review_summary:
The PR adds a staff publisher-abuse Signals dashboard backed by new Convex signal/archive tables, temporal signal archival, Hermit digest notifications, UI/tests, dev seed fixtures, and a security-moderation spec update.

Reproducibility: yes. for the PR defect: source inspection shows the digest emits `tab=signals` while the management route ignores `tab` and defaults the abuse tab to potential-ban nominations. The broader feature is not a current-main bug reproduction case.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair can wire and test the Signals deep link; maintainer policy acceptance remains a separate decision before merge.

target.title: Add publisher abuse signal review dashboard
target.body: ## Summary This PR turns selected temporal install/download anomalies into durable staff-review signals instead of letting temporal scoring drift into the ban-candidate workflow. The management abuse dashboard now has a Signals tab that shows archived anomaly evidence with severity, skill/publisher links, and install/download ratios, while warning-first autoban enforcement remains limited to pressure-score `potential_ban_candidate` nominations. The Signals tab count is backed by a bounded indexed read, and the signal list uses paginated backend queries so the management route does not reintroduce the Convex dashboard failures we saw earlier. ## What Changed - Temporal scoring: temporal anomaly labels stay review-only; pressure-score nominations remain the only automatic warning/ban input. - Signal archive: adds `publisherAbuseSignals` with indexed archival, listing, retention policy coverage, and local/dev seed fixtures. - Signal scope: archives high install/download-ratio evidence and sustained downloads-with-flat-installs evidence; spike-only one-day evidence is intentionally not archived as a durable Signals tab row. - Scheduled scan: the daily temporal scan remains a dry run, but explicitly opts into archiving staff-review signal rows. - Management UI: adds the Signals tab, severity column, skill/publisher links that open in a new tab, ratio columns, skeleton rows, stable tab counts, and tab-specific pagination skipping. ## Workflow | Step | Behavior | | --- | --- | | Daily pressure scoring | Existing publisher abuse scoring can still create pressure-score `potential_ban_candidate` nominations. | | Daily temporal scan | Runs as `dryRun: true` and only archives signal rows because the scheduled job explicitly opts in. | | Enforcement split | Pressure-score ban candidates continue through warning deadline / ban flow; temporal-only signals stay review evidence. | | Signal archive | High install/download ratio and sustained downloads with flat installs are upserted into `publisherAbuseSignals`. | | Spike-only evidence | Single spike-only temporal evidence is not archived as a durable Signals tab row. | | Management dashboard | Staff see a bounded Signals tab count, then paginate archived rows only after opening the Signals tab. | ## Proof Behavioral proof: - The seeded management fixture showed `Signals 2` before staff opened the Signals tab, proving the tab count comes from the dashboard query rather than from an already-loaded signal page. - Opening Signals showed two archived temporal signals with severity, linked skill/publisher context, and 7d/30d/all-time install/download ratios. - Backend tests cover the review-only temporal boundary, bounded dry-run signal archival, one-paginated-read signal listing, skipped staff/official publishers, and the intentional exclusion of spike-only evidence from durable signal rows. Screenshot proof: | Screenshot | Claim Proved | URL / State | Viewport / Crop | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | The dashboard can show `Signals 2` before staff open the Signals tab, while the other abuse tabs remain populated and not stuck in loading. | `http://127.0.0.1:3031/management?view=abuse`, local seeded fixture, signed in as `@local-admin`, Potential ban tab active. | Desktop `1440px` wide full-page capture, because the header metrics, tabs, table, and footer prove the whole management route state. | | | The Signals tab renders the severity column, linked skill/publisher cells, ratio columns, and the two seeded archived signal rows. | `http://127.0.0.1:3031/management?view=abuse`, local seeded fixture, signed in as `@local-admin`, Signals tab active. | Desktop `1440px` wide full-page capture, because the changed tab, table header, rows, and count are all visible together. | ## Verification Reviewer-checkable behavior: - `publisherAbuse:listReviewDashboard` returns the bounded signal count used by the tab; in the seeded fixture this renders as `Signals 2` before `listSignalsPage` is active. - `publisherAbuse:listSignalsPage` is skipped until the Signals tab is active, then pages archived signal rows for staff review. - `publisher-temporal-abuse-scan` remains `dryRun: true` and only archives dry-run signals because the cron explicitly passes `archiveDryRunSignals: true`. Automated checks run on the final pushed tree: - `bun run test -- convex/crons.test.ts convex/publisherAbuse.test.ts convex/publisherAbuseDevSeed.test.ts src/routes/-management.test.tsx convex/lib/publisherAbuseScoring.test.ts convex/lib/retentionPolicy.test.ts` passed: 6 files / 175 tests. - `bunx tsc --noEmit` passed. - `bunx convex dev --once --typecheck=disable` passed against dev deployment `admired-dodo-615`. - `bun run ci:static` passed. - `bun run ci:types-build` passed. - `bun run ci:unit` passed: 326 files passed / 1 skipped, 4241 tests passed / 1 skipped, coverage threshold passed. Proof-pack note: - Mermaid was intentionally omitted because the local Mermaid CLI could not launch its configured Chrome; the workflow is represented as a plain table instead.
